mainTopic: Counting the years of non-Jewish kings from תשרי, and the special case of כורש/דריוש
overview: The גמרא is proving that the years of a non-Jewish king are counted from תשרי, using two dates in ספר נחמיה. Both dates are called 'the twentieth year' of ארתחשסתא, one in כסלו and one in ניסן. רב פפא uses a גזירה שוה to show that both dates count the same king's reign. A ברייתא then shows that the כסלו event came first, so the year cannot have started in ניסן. רב יוסף challenges the rule from ספר חגי, where a date in תשרי is still 'the second year' of דריוש. רבי אבהו answers that כורש was a worthy king, so his years were counted from ניסן like the kings of ישראל. רב יוסף objects that the dates in ספר עזרא do not fit this, and that כורש is not דריוש. A ברייתא explains that כורש, דריוש and ארתחשסתא are one king, and רבי יצחק answers that he was counted from ניסן before he became corrupt and from תשרי afterward. רב כהנא begins to challenge whether he ever became corrupt, and his verse comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Maybe the כסלו date uses a different count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes a challenge: perhaps the 'twentieth year' mentioned with כסלו is counted by some other system, not by the reign of ארתחשסתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Perhaps the 'twentieth year' of כסלו] belongs to some other count?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge to the proof. It asks: maybe the 'twentieth year' in the כסלו פסוק is not counting ארתחשסתא's reign at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof only works if both dates use the same count, namely the years of ארתחשסתא. The כסלו פסוק (נחמיה א:א) says only 'the twentieth year' and does not name the king. So it could be counting something else, which would break the comparison with the ניסן פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: to a count / a system of counting years

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the end of a question that started on the previous amud. The full challenge is: 'How do we know this twentieth year is of ארתחשסתא? Maybe it belongs to another count?'

phrases.english: Is it [perhaps] according to another count?
phrases.notes: The end of a question that began in the previous lines of the גמרא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof (on the previous amud) that years of kings start in תשרי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the 'twentieth year' of כסלו is the twentieth year of ארתחשסתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כסלו פסוק never names the king. If it uses a different count, the two dates cannot be compared, and the proof falls apart.

steps.title: רב פפא links the two verses with a verbal analogy
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers with a גזירה שוה. The same phrase 'שנת עשרים' appears in both פסוקים, so both refer to ארתחשסתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: 'the twentieth year' appears here and 'the twentieth year' appears there. This is a גזירה שוה: just as there it means the twentieth year of ארתחשסתא, so too here it means the twentieth year of ארתחשסתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge. Since the same words appear in both פסוקים, we learn one from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ניסן פסוק (נחמיה ב:א) clearly says 'the twentieth year of ארתחשסתא.' Through a גזירה שוה, the identical phrase in the כסלו פסוק takes on the same meaning. Now both dates are on the same count, and the proof is back on track.

keyTerms.meaning: a rule of interpretation that links two places using the same word or phrase
just as there... so too here

steps.whyThisMatters: Without this link, the whole proof that kings' years start in תשרי would collapse.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
'The twentieth year' [here], 'the twentieth year' [there]: for a verbal analogy.
phrases.notes: The same phrase appears in נחמיה 1:1 and נחמיה 2:1.

phrases.english: Just as there it is of Artaxerxes,
phrases.notes: In the ניסן פסוק the king is named explicitly.

phrases.english: so too here it is of Artaxerxes.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual link through a גזירה שוה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כסלו date might use some unknown, different count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both dates count the reign of ארתחשסתא.

steps.title: Maybe the ניסן event came first
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge: even if both dates are in the same year of ארתחשסתא, how do we know the כסלו event came before the ניסן event?
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know the כסלו event came first? Maybe the ניסן event came first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second challenge to the proof. It asks how we know the order of the two events.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ניסן came first and כסלו came later in the same year, the year could still have started in ניסן. Then there would be no proof for תשרי. The proof only works if כסלו came before ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: and from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that the Kislev event came first?
Perhaps the Nisan event came first?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts that both dates use the same count, then attacks a different assumption: the order of events.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the כסלו event happened before the ניסן event.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ניסן came first, a year beginning in ניסן would fit both dates, so the proof for תשרי disappears.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the כסלו event came first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the challenge with a ברייתא: what חנני told נחמיה in כסלו, נחמיה later told the king in ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do not think that, because a ברייתא teaches: the words that חנני told נחמיה in כסלו, נחמיה told the king in ניסן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge. It brings a ברייתא showing that the כסלו event caused the ניסן event, so כסלו had to come first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחמיה could only report to the king news he had already heard. Since he heard it from חנני in כסלו and reported it in ניסן, כסלו came first. Since both dates are still 'the twentieth year,' the year did not begin in ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: חנני, נחמיה's relative who brought news from יהודה
נחמיה, a Jewish official in the Persian court

steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the logic: same year, כסלו first, then ניסן. So the year started earlier than ניסן, in תשרי.

phrases.english: It should not enter your mind, for it was taught [in a baraita]:
The words that Hanani said to Nehemiah in Kislev,
Nehemiah said them to the king in Nisan.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ניסן conversation passed on what was heard in כסלו, so כסלו came first.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a ברייתא that the כסלו report came before the ניסן conversation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ניסן event might have come before the כסלו event, so a year starting in ניסן would fit both dates.
steps.terutzMaskana: נחמיה told the king in ניסן what he had heard from חנני in כסלו, so כסלו came first within the same twentieth year.

steps.title: The ברייתא quotes the כסלו verses
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves its first half by quoting נחמיה 1:1–3. In כסלו of the twentieth year, חנני came to שושן and reported the terrible state of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words חנני said to נחמיה in כסלו are as the פסוק says: 'The words of נחמיה son of חכליה: It was in the month of כסלו, in the twentieth year, and I was in שושן the capital. חנני, one of my brothers, came, he and men from יהודה. I asked them about the Jews who had escaped, who were left from the captivity, and about ירושלים. They said to me: the ones who remain from the captivity there in the province are in great trouble and disgrace. The wall of ירושלים is broken through, and its gates were burned with fire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא starts proving its claim with a פסוק. Here it shows the first half: חנני spoke to נחמיה in כסלו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק clearly dates the conversation to כסלו of the twentieth year. It also spells out the news, so we can later see that this same news is what נחמיה brought to the king. The ניסן half of the proof will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is said (in the פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא repeating itself for nothing. The ברייתא is now proving each half of its statement from the פסוקים, starting with כסלו.

phrases.english: The words that Hanani said to Nehemiah in Kislev:
as it is said: 'The words of Nehemiah son of Hachaliah:
And it was in the month of Kislev, in the twentieth year,
and I was in Shushan the capital.
And Hanani, one of my brothers, came,
he and men from Judah,
and I asked them about the Jews who escaped,

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁאֲרוּ מִן הַשֶּׁבִי וְעַל יְרוּשָׁלִָם.
phrases.english: who remained from the captivity, and about Jerusalem.
And they said to me: Those who remain,

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁאֲרוּ מִן הַשְּׁבִי שָׁם בַּמְּדִינָה
phrases.english: who remained from the captivity, there in the province,
are in great trouble and disgrace,
and the wall of Jerusalem is broken through,
and its gates were burned with fire.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבָרִים שֶׁאָמַר חֲנָנִי לִנְחֶמְיָה בְּכִסְלֵיו שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא backs up the first half of its own statement from step 4 with a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That חנני's report to נחמיה happened in כסלו of the twentieth year.

steps.title: נחמיה repeats the news to the king in ניסן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves its second half by quoting נחמיה 2:1–6. In ניסן of the twentieth year, נחמיה told the king about ירושלים and asked permission to rebuild it.
steps.simpleTranslation: נחמיה told these words to the king in ניסן, as it says: 'In the month of ניסן, in the twentieth year of ארתחשסתא, I brought the king wine. He asked why my face was sad. I said: How can I not be sad when the city of my fathers' graves lies in ruins and its gates are burned? The king asked what I wanted. I asked him to send me to יהודה to rebuild it. He asked how long I would be gone, and he agreed to send me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא quotes the second set of פסוקים to show that נחמיה repeated חנני's report to the king in ניסן. This shows the ניסן conversation came after the כסלו report.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both stories are dated 'the twentieth year,' and the news clearly reached נחמיה (כסלו) before he told the king (ניסן). If the king's year began in ניסן, a כסלו that came earlier would belong to year nineteen. Since the כסלו event is still called year twenty, the new year for counting ארתחשסתא's reign must begin in תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: The graves of my fathers (a name for ירושלים here)
And I gave him a set time (for my return)

steps.whatToRemember: Same 'year twenty,' with כסלו before ניסן, means the reign of a non-Jewish king is counted from תשרי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This finishes the proof for the rule that non-Jewish kings' years are counted from תשרי. The next step challenges that rule.

phrases.english: Nehemiah told them (these words) to the king in Nisan,
as it is stated:
"And it was in the month of Nisan,
in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king,
phrases.notes: The same 'twentieth year' as the כסלו story

phrases.english: wine was before him,
and I lifted the wine and gave it to the king,
and I had never been sad in his presence before.
And the king said to me:
Why is your face sad
when you are not sick?

phrases.aramaic: אֵין זֶה כִּי אִם רֹעַ לֵב
phrases.english: This is nothing but sadness of the heart.
And I was very much afraid.
And I said to the king: May the king live forever!
Why should my face not be sad,

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר הָעִיר בֵּית קִבְרוֹת אֲבוֹתַי חֲרֵבָה
phrases.english: when the city, the place of my fathers' graves, lies in ruins,
phrases.notes: This is the same news חנני brought in כסלו

phrases.english: and its gates have been burned by fire?"
"And the king said to me:
What is it that you are asking for?
So I prayed to the God of heaven.

phrases.aramaic: וָאוֹמַר לַמֶּלֶךְ אִם עַל הַמֶּלֶךְ טוֹב
phrases.english: And I said to the king: If it pleases the king,
and if your servant has found favor before you,
please send me to Judah,
to the city of my fathers' graves, so that I may rebuild it.
And the king said to me,
with the queen sitting beside him:

phrases.aramaic: עַד מָתַי יִהְיֶה מַהֲלָכְךָ וּמָתַי תָּשׁוּב
phrases.english: How long will your journey take, and when will you return?
And it pleased the king to send me,
and I gave him a set time."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא's proof. Step 5 proved the כסלו half, and this step proves the ניסן half.
steps.raayaObject: That נחמיה told the king about ירושלים in ניסן of the same twentieth year, after hearing the news in כסלו

steps.title: רב יוסף challenges with dates from חגי
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף points out that ספר חגי calls both the 24th of the sixth month and the 21st of the seventh month 'the second year of דריוש.' If non-Jewish kings' years started in תשרי, the seventh-month date should already be year three.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: One פסוק says 'the 24th day of the sixth month, in the second year of דריוש,' and the next says 'in the seventh month, in the second year, on the 21st day.' If the king's year starts in תשרי, it should have said 'the seventh month, in the third year'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks the rule just proven, that a non-Jewish king's year begins in תשרי. He brings two dates from ספר חגי that seem to show the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sixth month is אלול and the seventh month is תשרי. If a new year of דריוש began on א׳ תשרי, then by כ״א תשרי it should be year three. The פסוק still says 'year two,' which suggests the year did not change at תשרי.

keyTerms.meaning: דריוש, the Persian king named in חגי
And if it were so (if your rule were true)

steps.confusionAlert: 'The sixth month' and 'the seventh month' are counted from ניסן, so they mean אלול and תשרי. The challenge is about crossing from אלול into תשרי without the year number changing.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection:
"On the twenty-fourth day of the month,
in the sixth month, in the second year of Darius,"
and it is written:
"In the seventh month, in the second year,
on the twenty-first of the month."
But if it were so (that the year starts in Tishrei),
it should have said "in the seventh month, in the third year"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion just proven in steps 4–6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the years of non-Jewish kings are counted from תשרי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two dates in חגי, one in אלול and one in תשרי, are both called 'year two' of דריוש. If his year began in תשרי, the second date should be 'year three.'

steps.title: כורש was a worthy king, so his years were counted from ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו answers that כורש was a worthy king. Because of this, his reign was counted from ניסן, like the kings of ישראל, so the year did not change in תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: כורש was a worthy king, so they counted his years like the years of the kings of ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers רב יוסף's challenge. This king was an exception, so the general rule did not apply to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that non-Jewish kings are counted from תשרי still stands. This king is a special case: because כורש was good, he was honored with the ניסן-based count used for the kings of ישראל. Under a ניסן count, both אלול and the following תשרי fall in 'year two,' so the פסוקים fit.

keyTerms.meaning: כורש, the Persian king who allowed the Jews to rebuild the בית המקדש
The kings of ישראל, whose years are counted from ניסן

steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק says דריוש, but רבי אבהו talks about כורש. The גמרא raises this exact problem in Step 10 and answers it in Step 11, so don't get stuck on it yet.
steps.whyThisMatters: It keeps the rule that non-Jewish kings are counted from תשרי. It only adds a special exception for a king who earned the honor of being counted like the kings of ישראל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
Cyrus was a worthy king,
therefore they counted his years like those of the kings of Israel.
phrases.notes: So they counted his years starting from ניסן.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: כּוֹרֶשׁ מֶלֶךְ כָּשֵׁר הָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רב יוסף's challenge in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Exception: this specific king was counted differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every non-Jewish king is counted from תשרי, so the תשרי date in חגי should be year three.
steps.terutzMaskana: The general rule stands. כורש, as a worthy king, was given the ניסן-based count of the kings of ישראל, so the תשרי date stays in year two.

steps.title: רב יוסף's first objection: the dates in ספר עזרא
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף argues that if this king's years started in ניסן, two verses in ספר עזרא would contradict each other. The arrival of עזרא would have to be in year eight, not year seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects with two arguments. First: if the king's years really started in ניסן, the verses contradict each other. One verse says the בית המקדש was finished on the 3rd of אדר in the sixth year of דריוש. A ברייתא says עזרא went up from בבל at that same time the next year. Another verse says עזרא arrived in ירושלים in the fifth month, in the seventh year of the king. If years started in ניסן, the verse should have said the eighth year.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges רבי אבהו's answer from Step 8. He shows that the dates in ספר עזרא only work if this king's years started in תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Start from אדר of year 6. If the new year began in ניסן, the next ניסן would start year 7, and the ניסן after that would start year 8. The following אב (the fifth month) would then fall in year 8. The verse says year 7, which only works if the year changed in תשרי. In that case אדר of year 6 is followed by תשרי (year 7), the next אדר is still year 7, and the next אב is still year 7, since תשרי has not come again.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objects to it (a forceful challenge)
And if it were so (if your claim were true)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two dates: the בית המקדש was finished in אדר of year 6, and עזרא arrived in אב of the FOLLOWING year. The whole question is whether that אב is year 7 or year 8.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef strongly objects to this:
One objection: that if so,
the verses contradict each other,
as it is written: "And this house was finished
on the third day of the month Adar,
which was the sixth year
of the reign of Darius the king",
and it was taught in a baraita: at that same time in the following year
Ezra went up from Babylonia with his group of exiles,
and it is written: "And he came to Jerusalem in the fifth month,
which was the seventh year of the king",
and if it were so (that his years started in Nisan),
it should have said "the eighth year."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אבהו's answer from Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's claim that this king's years were counted from ניסן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counting from ניסן would put עזרא's arrival in year 8, but the verse says year 7, which fits counting from תשרי.

steps.title: Second objection: כורש is not דריוש
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף adds a second objection: רבי אבהו's answer was about כורש, but the verses in חגי speak about דריוש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And further: are the cases comparable? There, רבי אבהו spoke about כורש, but here the verses speak about דריוש!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives his second objection: רבי אבהו's answer was about the wrong king.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו said כורש was worthy, so his years were counted from ניסן. The verses in question, however, name דריוש. Praise of כורש should not change how דריוש's years are counted.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it comparable? (Are these cases really alike?)

phrases.english: And further: is it comparable?
There it is Cyrus; here it is Darius!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is רב יוסף's second objection, added to the first one in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's use of כורש to explain verses about דריוש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The answer was given about a different king from the one named in the verses.

steps.title: A ברייתא: כורש, דריוש and ארתחשסתא are one king
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the second objection with a ברייתא. כורש, דריוש and ארתחשסתא are three names for the same man.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: he is כורש, he is דריוש, he is ארתחשסתא. He was called כורש because he was a worthy (כשר) king. He was called ארתחשסתא after his kingdom (a royal title). And what was his real name? דריוש was his name.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא removes רב יוסף's second objection by showing that כורש and דריוש are the same person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since all three names refer to one king, what רבי אבהו said about כורש also applies to דריוש. The ברייתא explains each name: כורש is a description (from כשר, worthy), ארתחשסתא is his royal title, and דריוש is his actual name.

keyTerms.meaning: Worthy, proper (the wordplay behind the name כּוֹרֶשׁ)

steps.confusionAlert: This answers ONLY the second objection (Step 10). The first objection about year 7 versus year 8 is not resolved here. Step 12 brings it back, and רבי יצחק answers it in Step 13.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita: he is Cyrus,
he is Darius, he is Artaxerxes.
Cyrus (Koresh), because he was a worthy (kasher) king;
Artaxerxes, after his kingdom (his royal title);
and what was his name? Darius was his name.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הוּא כּוֹרֶשׁ, הוּא דָּרְיָוֶשׁ, הוּא אַרְתַּחְשַׁסְתְּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second objection from Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identification: the two names refer to one person
steps.terutzHavaAmina: כורש and דריוש were different kings, so praise of כורש does not apply to דריוש.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are the same king, so רבי אבהו's point about כורש applies to the verses about דריוש.

steps.title: The first objection still stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that even after the names are explained, the contradiction between the verses remains.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reminds us that the first objection (Step 9) is still unanswered, and sets up רבי יצחק's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know it is one king, the problem is even sharper. In ספר חגי his years seem to be counted from ניסן, but in ספר עזרא they seem to be counted from תשרי. How can the same king be counted two different ways?

keyTerms.meaning: The two possible starting points of the year (background terms)

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the second objection is answered, the גמרא returns to the first objection from Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the same king's years were counted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One king's years appear to start in ניסן in חגי but in תשרי in עזרא.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: before and after the king became corrupt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק explains that while the king was good, his years were counted from ניסן. After he became corrupt, they were counted from תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: It is not difficult. Here (in חגי, counting from ניסן) it speaks of the time before he became corrupt. There (in עזרא, counting from תשרי) it speaks of the time after he became corrupt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק resolves the contradiction by splitting the king's reign into two time periods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The honor of counting from ניסן depended on the king being worthy. Early in his reign (the second year, in חגי) he was good, so his years were counted from ניסן. Later (years 6–7, in עזרא) he went bad and lost that honor, so his years were counted from תשרי like other non-Jewish kings.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)
Became sour, meaning he became corrupt

steps.whatToRemember: One king, two ways of counting: from ניסן while he was worthy, from תשרי after he became corrupt.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said: it is not difficult:
here it is before he became corrupt (soured),
there it is after he became corrupt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty restated in Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by time period (before and after a change in the king)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One king must have one fixed way of counting his years.
steps.terutzMaskana: The counting changed when the king changed from worthy to corrupt.

steps.title: רב כהנא asks: did he really become corrupt?
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא challenges רבי יצחק by questioning whether the king ever became corrupt. He begins to cite a verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא strongly objects: Did he really become corrupt? But it is written:
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא attacks רבי יצחק's answer and starts to quote a verse. The verse itself comes in the next part of the גמרא, so this line sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק's answer depends on the king turning bad between the second year and the seventh year. רב כהנא is about to bring a verse suggesting the king was still acting well at that later time. If so, the answer of "he became corrupt" falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Did he really become corrupt? (a challenging question)
But isn't it written...? (introduces a contradicting verse)

phrases.english: Rav Kahana strongly objects to this:
Did he really become corrupt?
But isn't it written:
phrases.notes: The verse continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא: וּמִי הֶחְמִיץ? וְהָכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יצחק's answer from Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק's claim that the king became corrupt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A verse (quoted next) suggests the king did not become corrupt, so the before/after split has no basis.
